text_blocks.snippet: While the NFT market has experienced a significant downturn since its peak, some NFTs still hold considerable value, but the vast majority are reportedly worth very little or nothing. The market saw a massive bubble burst, with many NFTs plummeting in value, and a large percentage now considered "dead".

list.title: Market Crash:
list.snippet: The NFT market has seen a dramatic decline, with a reported 95% of NFTs now considered worthless, according to a report from ARTnews.com.

list.title: Reduced Trading Volume:
list.snippet: Trading volume for NFTs has plummeted, with weekly trading values now a small fraction of their peak in 2021, according to a report from Cartoon Brew.

list.title: Losses for Owners:
list.snippet: Many NFT owners have experienced significant losses on their investments, with some reports citing average losses around 44.5%.

list.title: Factors Contributing to Decline:
list.snippet: The bubble burst, driven by speculation and hype, played a significant role. Additionally, concerns about market manipulation, fraud, and the lack of clear legal frameworks for NFTs have also contributed to the decline.

list.title: Exceptions:
list.snippet: Despite the overall downturn, some NFTs, particularly those associated with high-profile projects or unique digital art, continue to retain value.

list.title: Future Outlook:
list.snippet: While the initial hype has faded, there is still some interest in NFTs, particularly as a way to represent digital ownership of assets. Companies are still exploring potential use cases for blockchain technology and NFTs, but the market is more focused on practical applications than speculative trading.
